text:
Amanda: heads up, getting a bunch of p99 latency complaints from a customer on prod-us-east for model-xtreme-8k since the 03:10 deploy. p95 up too but p99 is the killer, ~2.2s vs usual 600ms. no errors returned, just slow responses.
Priya: thanks — are these dedicated customers or hosted? any request ids?
Amanda: hosted. I pasted the sample request ids in the ticket: rids: r-48211, r-48219. pattern: long prompts (~4k tokens), beam-style responses.
Dave: oncall here, pulling traces. I see kernel selection logs around the same time as the deploy. searching for compile flags changed.
ops-bot: deploy finished: runtime-service v2026-03-16.23 -> canary 20% -> stable 100% (commit: a3f9c2e).
Priya: that commit touched attention kernel heuristics + added a new compile flag `ENABLE_SDPA_HEURISTIC`. maybe related.
Lin: grabbing kernel logs from host-12: `KernelSelector: model=xtreme-8k seq=4096 selected=sdpa_compat reason=heuristic_score(0.78) vs flashopt(0.74)`
Lin: note: before deploy flashopt was winning for these seq distributions. now sdpa_compat chosen more often. SDPA path is slower for this model on A100 with our current kernels (regression introduced).
Jen: can we repro locally with same flags? running the reproduce script on a longseq trace now.
Priya: repro steps for others: ```python reproduce.py --model xtreme-8k --seq 4096 --batch 1 --flags ENABLE_SDPA_HEURISTIC=1```
Jen: confirmed — p99 jumps to ~2.1s when flag=1, stays ~600ms when flag=0.
Dave: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback the deploy 2) flip heuristic flag off via runtime dynamic flag 3) add a temporary override to prefer flashopt for seq>=2048. which is fastest to push?
Priya: we can toggle the runtime feature flag quickly. I can flip `sdpa_heuristic` to `off` for prod-us-east. doing it now.
Priya: `ops:feature-flag set sdpa_heuristic false --env prod-us-east`
ops-bot: feature-flag updated: sdpa_heuristic=false (effective: 30s)
Lin: metrics already trending back down. p99 dropping towards baseline within one minute.
Amanda: customer reports improvement in ticket. sending update. :thumbsup:
Maya: tagged as high priority customer, will follow up with CS to offer credit for the disruption.
Priya: root cause: the new heuristic inadvertently favored SDPA-compatible kernels for long sequences due to a weight change in the scoring function; combined with a compile variance in SDPA kernel that regressed perf on the A100 microcode we run. Patch is needed in two places: kernel scoring normalization + a micro-optimization in the SDPA kernel.
Dave: scope: need hotfix for scoring immediately, then a kernel recompile later. I'll open the hotfix PR.
Priya: PR opened: https://git.redwood.ai/runtime/merge_requests/812 (title: normalize-kernel-score-longseq). tagging Lin for review.
Lin: quick review done, merging. will roll as a canary patch.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: runtime-service v2026-03-16.23-hotfix1 -> 5%
Lin: canary metrics look good. promoting to 50%.
deploy-bot: canary promoted -> stable 100%
Jen: deploy confirmed. kernel selection logs show flashopt wins again for seq>=2048.
Amanda: customer confirmed stable performance in the ticket. closing on their side.
Priya: followups: 1) full SDPA kernel recompile job scheduled (CI queue) 2) add unit test for kernel scoring edgecases 3) update release notes + postmortem.
Maya: thanks team. I'll coordinate CS messaging.
Dave: tagging postmortem owner. assigning to Priya. ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.
Priya: will include timelines, metrics, and the mitigation playbook (feature-flag flip, rollback steps, reproduce commands).
Amanda: nice work all.
Jen: note for runbook: prefer feature-flag toggle as first mitigation if kernel-selection misbehaves — faster than rollback. adding to runbook now.
Priya: closing thread once postmortem is up.
Amanda: thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
